stem:
Diya hears that elephants have entered farms and villages in several parts of India after forest cover fell, vegetation became scarce, rainfall patterns changed, and waterholes dried in the natural habitat. Animals may move in search of food and water when those resources are not plentiful.

Which claim best explains why the animals moved?

options.text: When vegetation becomes scarce and waterholes dry in the natural habitat, elephants move into farms and villages in search of food and water.
Elephants prefer villages for company even when forest food and water are plentiful.
Farms and villages create extra forest cover and fuller waterholes, which draw the elephants in.
Rainfall, forest cover, and waterholes have no link to where elephants find food and water.

teacher.key_rationale: Resource shortage in the natural habitat drives movement into farms and villages. Preferring villages while resources remain plentiful drops the scarcity condition. Saying farms create forest and water reverses cause and effect. Denying any link stretches past the habitat-resource rule.
